title: Pair two sequences safely
prompt:
Write `pair_totals(names, amounts)` returning a list of `(name, amount)` tuples.

The two inputs must be the same length: if they are not, raise `ValueError`. Do not silently ignore extra items — that is the bug this exercise is about.

starter_files.main.py:
def pair_totals(names: list[str], amounts: list[int]) -> list[tuple[str, int]]:
    """Zip names with amounts, refusing mismatched lengths."""
    # Your code here
    ...

hints.text: `zip` stops at the shorter input by default — which is exactly the silent behaviour the prompt forbids.
Since Python 3.10 `zip` takes `strict=True`, which raises ValueError on a length mismatch.
`list(...)` around the zip turns the iterator into the list the tests compare against.

solution.explanation: `strict=True` is the whole exercise. An explicit length check first would also pass, but this states the requirement where the pairing happens instead of somewhere a later edit can drift away from.
